title: Be Kind to Who You Were Then
core_idea: Accepting your younger self means remembering that you acted with what you knew and could carry at the time; hindsight was never available to them.
text: It is easy to look back and wince. Why did I stay so long? Why didn't I speak up? Why did I believe that? But the person you were then did not have what you have now. They didn't have the hindsight, the lessons, the years that taught you. They had only that moment, that fear, that hope, and whatever strength they could find. Looking back with clearer eyes is a gift. It doesn't have to become a weapon. Try picturing your younger self the way you would picture a friend in a hard season. Not perfect. Not foolish. Simply doing their best with what they could carry. You are here partly because they kept going.
description: A gentle reflection on accepting your younger self, who acted with only what they knew and could carry at the time.
